findings.title: The "numpy" backend would time Numba kernels, and the Numba runner is assigned to a slice that comes after its consumer
findings.description:
The design says NumPy is "the only backend that exists today" (lines 25-26) and defers the Numba runner to "slice 144 / 118 territory" (lines 92, 341-343, 589-591). The code says otherwise:

- Slice 118 is complete (`100-slices.behavior-engine.md:61` is `[x]`) and `numba>=0.60` is a hard dependency (`pyproject.toml:11`).
- `USE_JIT_KERNELS` defaults to `True`, and every force except `PropulsionForce` dispatches to `forces_jit` through it (`flocking.py:82,192,326`, `herding.py:32,175`).

Consequences if implemented as written:

- **Mislabelled results.** Every JSON record with `"backend": "numpy"` holds Numba force timings. The design never says the runner sets the flag.
- **Wrong golden.** The "NumPy run is the golden" hash (lines 465-467) would be a Numba hash.
- **Invalid sanity check.** Walkthrough step 9 (lines 661-668) compares against the architecture's `force_total` 3.14 ms, which is the NumPy `reduceat` number (arch line 55).
- **Slice 142 is blocked.** The plan defines 142 as benchmarking "against the existing NumPy and Numba implementations" with dependencies (141) and (118) (plan line 30). No slice before 142 owns a `numba` runner, and 144 is the Quadrants force port.
- **Plan wording.** "Numba and Quadrants slot in as those backends become available" (plan line 26) — Numba is available now.

Fix: register both `numpy` and `numba` in this slice; they are the same runner with the flag forced `False` or `True`. State where the process-global flag is set and restored (setup / `finalize` in a `finally`), since `--all-backends` runs both in one process. Record the flag in the JSON.

findings.title: The workload schema is 3-D; the engine and the existing loader are 2-D
findings.description:
The example workload uses `world_size: [200.0, 200.0, 200.0]` and 3-component `cluster_centers` (design lines 366-368). The code is 2-D throughout:

- `DIMS = 2`, and `AgentState.create` allocates `(n, DIMS)` (`state.py:52-54`).
- Every JIT kernel hard-codes two columns (`forces_jit.py:43`).
- The loader already in the repo rejects anything but 2 entries (`bench/workload.py:187-191`), pinned by `test_world_size_must_be_2d` (`tests/bench/test_workload.py:122-128`).

`mid-flock.yaml` as written raises `ValueError` at load. Walkthrough steps 3, 5 and 6 and the first functional criterion (lines 550-552) therefore cannot run as written. The schema is declared stable for downstream slices (line 529), so the design has to be corrected, not just the YAML.

findings.title: Per-force timings are assigned to this slice by the plan and deferred to 142
findings.description:
The plan entry lists "force totals per force" among the phases this slice reports (plan line 26). The design ships one `force_total` number and pushes the breakdown to 142.

That deferral contradicts the design's own integration contract. Slice 142 would have to extend `PhaseTimings`, bump `schema_version` and change both reporters. That is not "one file … zero changes elsewhere in the harness" (lines 586-588), and the schema is not "stable from this slice" (line 530).

The cost of doing it now is one timer pair per iteration: the force loop is already per-force (`tick.py:110-111`). Put `force_breakdown` in schema v1.

findings.title: The parity hash cannot do the cross-backend job the design gives it
findings.description:
- **No tolerance is possible.** Slice 145's parity is "within a documented tolerance" (plan lines 36, 78). A SHA-256 cannot be "interpreted within a tolerance band" (lines 471-473); it is equal or not.
- **Always different across backends.** The repo's own Numba-vs-NumPy parity is `assert_allclose(atol=1e-12, rtol=1e-9)`, not bit equality (`tests/test_forces_jit_parity.py:7,200`). After 660 ticks, hashes will differ between any two backends, so the field carries no information for 142/144/145 (lines 533-534).
- **Two definitions.** Scope hashes the "post-warmup" state (line 81); this section hashes "after the measure phase" (line 460).
- **Padding.** `TickResult.count` may be less than `positions.shape[0]` on a GPU backend (`tick_result.py:95-98`). The hash must cover `[:count]`; the design hashes whole arrays.

Fix: keep the hash as a same-backend fingerprint, and write the final arrays as an `.npz` sidecar for tolerance comparison. Alternatively point cross-backend parity at `tools/run_deterministic_trajectory.py`, which already saves exactly that.

findings.title: Data flow reads the final `TickResult` after `finalize()`
findings.description: The diagram runs `finalize()` → `TickResult (final state)` → `parity.hash(result)`. `finalize` is the hook that releases GPU memory (line 338) and returns `None` (line 333). A `TickResult` is valid only until the next tick and may be backed by recycled buffers (`tick_result.py:47-55`). On any non-NumPy backend this hashes released memory. Hash before `finalize`, and call `finalize` in a `finally`.

findings.title: The design says the runner calls `tick()` and also that it never does
findings.description:
Lines 60, 131-132 and 541 say the NumPy runner calls `engine.tick.tick` directly. Decision B (lines 255-267, 498-501) has it run a re-implemented `tick_instrumented`. Under B the harness never times production `tick()`.

The only guard is one bit-equality test (lines 688-690). `tick()` has two neighbor paths, selected by whether every profile sets `max_neighbors` (`tick.py:72-102`), plus the `active_indices` branch. The test must cover each path, and the design names none.

A lighter option the design does not weigh: pass timing proxies for the `SpatialQuery` and each `BulkForce` into the real `tick()`. That gives build, query and per-force timings with no duplication, leaving only CSR assembly and integrate as a remainder.

findings.title: "Add one file, zero changes elsewhere" does not hold for a decorator registry
findings.description:
`@register_backend` runs only when the module is imported, and the design never says who imports backend modules. `backends/__init__.py` is currently a one-line stub. The two ways to do it both break a stated criterion:

- **Explicit import in `backends/__init__.py`:** every new backend edits a second file, breaking lines 586-591.
- **Package auto-discovery:** importing a Quadrants backend on a machine without Quadrants (lines 93-95 say 141 must not require it) raises `ImportError` from `--list-backends` and from every run.

Specify discovery, with a failed import listed as "unavailable: <reason>" rather than aborting.

findings.title: The Markdown report reads the whole results directory, which a bad file can block
findings.description:
"One table per workload across all backends in `bench/results/`" means the renderer reads every prior JSON.

- **Duplicates.** After the walkthrough's re-run (step 5) there are two `mid-flock`/`numpy` files. Which one is the row is not stated, and step 3 expects exactly "one numpy row" (line 619).
- **Mixed provenance.** Rows from different commits and machines land in one table, unlabelled.
- **Stuck state.** A JSON truncated by a kill mid-write, or one with a newer `schema_version` (which readers "must reject", line 532), fails the report step of every later run until someone deletes the file by hand.
- **Unnamed output.** The `.md` filename is never given (line 220).

Fix: render only the records produced by the current invocation, write JSON via temp file and rename, and skip unreadable files with a warning.

findings.title: `tps_observed`, `wall_seconds` and `total_ns` are undefined, and the example contradicts itself
findings.description:
- The example has `tps_observed` 65.1, which is 600 / 9.21 s. Mean `total_ns` is 9.55 ms, which is 104.7 TPS and 5.73 s for 600 ticks. About 3.5 s of wall time is unexplained (warmup, progress output, hashing?).
- The Markdown row shows TPS 65.1 beside a 9.40 ms median total (line 447).
- `total_ns` "includes density-record dispatch" (lines 287-289), which runs after integrate (`tick.py:129-130`). The `PhaseTimings` docstring already in the repo ends it at integrate (`bench/runner.py:27-28`).
- "Sortable on TPS" (line 80) is not something a Markdown table does; say rows are ordered by TPS.

A schema declared stable needs these three definitions pinned.

findings.title: Provenance is too thin for the cross-run, cross-machine comparison the slice promises
findings.description:
- **No dirty flag.** `git rev-parse HEAD` attributes numbers to a commit even when the tree has uncommitted changes, which is the normal state when benchmarking a change. That defeats "reproducible by repo hash + workload name" (lines 184-185).
- **No CPU identity.** `platform.processor()` is `"arm"` on Apple Silicon (the design's own example, line 422), so the record cannot distinguish one Mac from another.
- **Missing fields.** There is no NumPy/SciPy/Numba version, JIT flag, spatial backend name, device/arch field for Metal vs CUDA, or hash of the workload file content.
- **Unhandled path.** The git subprocess failing (no git, not a checkout) is not covered.

findings.title: How a workload becomes an `AgentState` is unspecified, and the report cannot show which regime ran
findings.description:
- **Schema vs scope.** Scope promises "density", "formation seed" and "RNG seed" fields (lines 70-72). The schema has one `seed` and no density.
- **Initial velocities.** Not stated. If zero, `MomentumForce` takes its skip branch (`forces_jit.py:164-165`).
- **Leadership is degenerate.** Per-agent `state.leadership` is zero-initialised (`state.py:71`) and the schema cannot set it. Every row hits `lead_sum < 1e-10 → continue` (`forces_jit.py:212-213`), so the leadership force is timed on a path that does no work.
- **`max_neighbors`.** Not stated. It selects the tick path (`tick.py:72-102`), and the architecture's reference uses k=13.
- **Sampling.** Profile assignment by fraction (rounding, order) and the cluster distribution are undefined, yet the parity hash depends on both.
- **Regime drift.** The harness applies no bounds policy, and 660 ticks will move a packed or dispersed start away from its named regime.
- **Nothing recorded.** The plan requires the "formation-dependent breakdown" (plan line 26), but the report records no realised density. Mean neighbors per agent is already computed as the CSR counts (`tick.py:103`); emit it.

findings.title: Several statements about existing code are wrong
findings.description:
- **"Five existing `BulkForce` implementations" (lines 138-139, 543).** There are six weight-driven forces; `PropulsionForce` exists (`herding.py:102`) and the plan lists it for 144 (plan line 34). `config/default.yaml:173-176` enables propulsion, so the "default operating point" workload omits a force the server runs. The loader already in the repo registers it (`bench/workload.py:73`).
- **"Module-level singleton instances (e.g. `flocking.cohesion_force`)" (lines 398-399).** None exist; there are only classes (`flocking.py:65`).
- **"`engine.spatial.KDTreeQuery` — the spatial backend used today" (line 542).** The class is at `migratory/spatial/kd_tree.py:16`, and there is no `engine.spatial`. The server default is `adaptive` (`migratory_server/config.py:293`); kdtree is opt-in.
- **Profile "presets" in `migratory.engine.profile`, "used in `config/default.yaml`", "does not invent new profiles" (lines 371, 392-395).** `profile.py` holds only the dataclass. `default.yaml` defines a single profile named `default` (line 146). `leader` is invented (`bench/workload.py:30-31`).
- **`mid-flock` "roughly equivalent to the live-server default config" (lines 353-355).** `default.yaml` is 100 agents on 1000×1000 at 20 TPS (lines 8-9, 23, 262).
- **Risk: `all_radii` setup inflates `force_total` at small N (lines 697-702).** That line is `tick.py:58`, before the spatial query and outside the force loop (`tick.py:109-111`). The Python work inside `force_total` is the per-agent weight list comprehension in each force (e.g. `flocking.py:108-111`), which is O(n) per force and grows with N.
- **Phase names (lines 246-248).** The architecture's table calls the third phase `self_excl_cap` and counts 4 forces (arch lines 54-55). `KDTreeQuery.query_knn_batch` also does its own per-row flat assembly (`kd_tree.py:206-222`), so `csr_assembly` will not capture all assembly cost.
- **"New package: `src/migratory/bench/`" (line 155).** It already exists with `runner.py`, `workload.py`, a placeholder `cli.py` and `tests/bench/`. The design should say what is kept; for example, the diagram's `workload.load()` (line 192) is `Workload.from_yaml` in the code.

findings.title: The CLI section does not define the flags the walkthrough uses, and the entry point discards the exit code
findings.description:
- `--list-backends` and `--list-workloads` (lines 605, 611) are not in the CLI section.
- The third form, `--workload-dir bench/workloads --backend numpy` with no `--workload`, has no stated meaning.
- `--all-backends` has no stated ordering or isolation.
- Paths are relative to the working directory, so a run from a subdirectory finds no workloads and writes results elsewhere.
- `__main__.py:5-6` calls `main()` and drops its return value, so the "non-zero on failure" contract (line 485) needs `sys.exit(main())`.
- Walkthrough steps 4 and 5 call bare `python` (lines 625, 637), which is not on PATH in a uv project on macOS; use `uv run python`.

findings.title: The failure-mode list covers four cases and misses the paths that leave partial state
findings.description:
Not covered:

- `tick_once` raising, or Ctrl-C, mid-measure: is `finalize` called, and is anything written?
- `finalize` raising inside the `finally` and masking the original error.
- `finalize` on a backend whose `setup` failed halfway.
- An empty YAML file: `yaml.safe_load` returns `None`, and the existing loader then raises `TypeError` at `bench/workload.py:134-135` instead of the promised clear message.
- Fractions not summing to 1; `n <= 0`.
- `measure_ticks: 0`: `aggregate` raises only after the warmup has run (`bench/runner.py:63-64`); validate at load.
- Results directory unwritable; git subprocess failure.

findings.title: Some mechanisms have no user in this slice and can be cut
findings.description:
- **Persisted `.md` file (line 220).** Stdout is what the walkthrough reads, and the file's name and overwrite rule are unspecified.
- **`pytest-benchmark` for stub-backend tests (lines 122-124).** The existing stub in `tests/bench/conftest.py` does not use it and the tests assert on synthetic integers.
- **"Old readers must reject unknown versions" (line 532).** No reader exists.
- **Walkthrough step 10.** It `cat`s a source file and proves nothing.
- **Value section (lines 36-51).** It restates the plan entry.

findings.title: Count pins could not be verified, and one criterion contradicts the file list
findings.description:
- "1100 passed, 2 skipped" and "433 pre-existing pyright errors" were not checked.
- `tests/bench/` already holds harness tests at HEAD, so "existing 1100 + N new" (line 658) has no clean baseline.
- "All new code lives under `src/migratory/bench/` and `bench/workloads/`" (line 574) omits `tests/bench/` and the `.gitignore` entry (already present at `.gitignore:172-174`).

findings.title: Layering, dependency direction and prerequisites are correct
findings.description:
- The harness depends on `migratory.engine` and `migratory.spatial` and excludes `migratory_server`, matching the "wire is a separate problem" principle (arch line 46). The scaffold's imports already follow this.
- Slice 140 is complete and `tick()` returns `TickResult` (`tick.py:22`).
- `pyyaml` and `pytest-benchmark` are present (`pyproject.toml:14,73`).
- The out-of-scope list (CUDA CI, wire benchmarks, regression gating) matches the plan's "standalone against NumPy at first".
- Step 9's reference numbers match the architecture (arch lines 52-56).
- No architecture NFR applies to this path.
